question: Should OpenClaw commit to local, container, reverse-proxy, and node-mode as permanent core, release-tested hosting profiles with public config, CLI, environment, readiness, and support contracts?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and proven, but code review cannot decide which deployment postures OpenClaw promises to support as named core products or whether that long-lived surface is worth the compatibility and release burden.

options.title: Approve the four-profile matrix
options.body: Land the readiness dependency first, then accept all four opt-in profiles and their release conformance as the initial supported core matrix.

options.title: Narrow the initial matrix
options.body: Accept only the clearly bounded local, container, and reverse-proxy profiles while deferring node-mode until its control-plane support contract is separately approved.

options.title: Keep direct criteria only
options.body: Decline named core profiles and retain operator-selected readiness criteria as the supported low-level mechanism.

recommendation.title: Approve the four-profile matrix
recommendation.body: Land the readiness dependency first, then accept all four opt-in profiles and their release conformance as the initial supported core matrix.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent core/plugin boundary and Gateway policy history makes them the strongest available owner for the permanent product-contract choice.
